steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Make crust: Transfer 1 cup cake mix to a small bowl; set aside for topping. Place remaining cake mix in a medium bowl with melted butter and egg; mix until well blended.
Spread mixture into the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Make filling: Combine pumpkin puree, eggs, milk, brown sugar, and pumpkin pie spice in a large bowl; mix well and pour over crust.
Make topping: Add white sugar and cubed butter to reserved cake mix; use a pastry blender to mix until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Sprinkle over pumpkin filling, then scatter chopped walnuts over the top.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is golden brown, 45 to 50 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Pumpkin Dessert
raw_recipe.description: Pumpkin desserts come in a variety of forms but this one takes the cake! Cake mix stands in for pastry crust in this delicious alternative to pumpkin pie.
raw_recipe.name: Pumpkin Dessert

review.reviewBody: Good recipe. I used the canned pumpkin that already has spices and sugar in it. I might add a bit more spice next time, but it was fine as is. This recipe was good out of the oven but tasted MUCH better the next morning. If I were to make it again I would allow at least 12 hours before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.

VERY good! Our family loves pumpkin EVERYTHING and this is no exception. We all prefer this over pumpkin pie! It makes a large pan (great for potlucks or bigger crowds) but could easily be halved.
Do serve it warm with whipped cream.
I made this exactly as is with 2 exceptions: 
1. Substituted pecans in place of walnuts
2. Made a "from scratch" boxed cake mix to sub for the store-bought boxed cake mix (just not a fan of those). Here is the recipe I used for the boxed cake mix substitute:
Ingredients:
2 1/2 cups (320 g) all-purpose flour
1 1/2 cup (300 g) sugar
4 tsp baking powder
1/4 cup (60 g) butter or vegetable shortening or margarine
1/3 tsp salt
Directions:
Sift all dry ingredients and put into food processor. Add room temp butter/shortening and mix until the consistency of dry cake mix (a fine powder). 
Making this again, I will cut down on the butter in the topping (I had to mix a little extra flour to get the topping to a crumbly consistency mixing it in the food processor). Also I will add more spices (pumpkin pie spice, nutmeg and cinnamon).
Used pumpkin pie spices and ginger for extra zing! Less sugar, a hit with everyone

We had not yet had any pumpkin dessert for Christmas so I decided to try this recipe. I made this recipe only sugar free. I used a sugar free 16ounce yellow cake mix. Changed all of the sugar to Splenda - in the pumpkin part I used a cup of Splenda and added a teaspoon of molasses to substitute for brown sugar. I used 1/2 cup Splenda in the topping part. I also changed the spice some for the pumpkin part to 4 teaspoons of pumpkin pie spice and 1/2 teaspoon each of cinnamon and nutmeg. I also used half and half instead of milk. I then baked this until a knife came out clean in the center. It was delicious!! The only thing I would change next time is I would double the pumpkin mixture so that there is more pumpkin in the middle - with the original recipe there is only about 1/2 to 3/4 inch of pumpkin mixture and the cake mixture on the bottom was close to 1/2 thick - I wanted more pumpkin between the top and bottom layers -- will definitely make this again -- sugar free and with more pumpkin!! I don't think I will make pumpkin pie again either -- I really like this as a great substitute for pie.

This recipe adapts BEAUTIFULLY to gluten-free/dairy-free.

I did not have any gluten-free cake mix, so I went to my gf cook-book, looked up a recipe for yellow cake, and used the dry ingredients as my "cake mix." (2.5 c gf flour w/xanthan gum, 2 c sugar, 1 T baking powder, 1/4 t salt)

I subbed coconut oil for the butter, and oat milk for the milk. Coconut milk would have been my first choice, but we didn't have any.

I also followed others' advice, added vanilla extract to the pumpkin layer, and used brown sugar instead of white for the topping.

I may have added an extra half-cup of walnuts. Possibly two.

This is SO good, we may not have any left over to see if it's better the second day. The gluten-eaters and dairy-eaters in our family could not tell it was gluten-free or dairy free.

I'd give this 10 stars if I could.

YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM YUM

I didn't read all 140 reviews so if someone has already suggested this I'm sorry. Like other reviewers I added vanilla extract (a couple of dashes) to the crust and filling. I also added 1 pkg of jello pumpkin pudding, 1 dash nutmeg, 1 dash pumpkin pie spice, 1 dash ground cloves, and 1 dash powdered ginger. I also used brown sugar instead of white sugar for topping. The key is letting it sit for a coupla hours. Don't serve just made. This is awesome & easy!!! Definitely could be made the day before and served at room temp. Thanks for the recipe!!!
Made this for company. Everyone raved about it! I cut sugar in topping to 1/4 cup. It was plenty sweet. I also used 2-1/2 T of Penzeys Cake Spice mix instead of the individual spices. A keeper!

Excellent recipe. I didn't have a yellow cake mix, so I used white instead and baked a real pumpkin and used fresh pumpkin instead of canned. It turned out excellent. Thank you for this great pumpkin dessert recipe. It's a keeper. I'm gong to make it again for Thanksgiving.

This got raves when i served it at my Circle meeting. Can't give it 5 stars because it took an hour to bake. I carefully read all the reviews and made some changes accordingly. Probably not fair to review it since I made so many changes. Crust: used 1/4 c butter, egg white only, added 1/3 c light brown sugar, 1/2 teas vanilla. Was not easily spreadable, so next time I will try the whole egg and 1/3 c butter. Pumpkin layer: used 30 oz can pumpkin pie mix and 2 eggs. Top layer I mixed all this together, including the nuts: reserved cake mix, 1/4 c chilled butter, 1/4 c sugar, 1/8 c light brown sugar, 1/4 c regular oatmeal, 1/8 teas cinnamon, 1/8 teas nutmeg, 1/2 c chopped walnuts. Baked for one hour. Made it the night before and put in fridge overnight. It is pie consistency, so needs forks.

Very good. I used half the amount if white sugar for the topping, and it turned out perfect. I probably should’ve cooked it for another five minutes. Next time, I think I’ll try and bake the crust a bit before adding the rest of the layers, to crisp it up a bit.

Amazing recipe, quick and a welcome change to pumpkin pie. Only two items of note that I changed: I added a bit more butter and a splash of water to the base as it was NOT cooperating. Could have been the brand of boxed that I was working with, (idk because I never use boxed cake) but using the recipe as written- the base was far too crumbly to assemble into the bottom of the pan. Additionally,I used my own pumpkin pie mix, as I always make a big batch from scratch each holiday season and in 2023 I bought too large a pumpkin for my crowd. Will definitely be introducing to the 2024 holiday rotation.
So easy to make. Didn't change anything!
Warning!!! These are addictive. My morning coffee isn't the same since I finished off this recipe. Had to make another batch tonight for a 3 day week-end
Did not change anything and it was perfect!!!!
I am not a level type woman so I just put it all together. It was amazing with white frosting. Thanks for great recipe.
The directions were a little hard to understand, but a overall nice dessert and was perfect warm with whipped cream!
I was surprised by the high ratings. The pumpkin flavor was very mild. The recipe was okay but I won't be repeating. We served with ice cream on the side, but it still wasn't worth the calories.
It was an excellent dessert for any time you want a pumpkin dessert but can't replace pie on holidays.

I had a random box of yellow cake mix in the pantry. I googled a recipe that I could use it in. I found this one, made it and we absolutely loved it! A spoonful of vanilla ice cream topped it off! Congrats on a stellar desert! Will definitely make this again!
